newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $65, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $65, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids at $65.00 per cwt early Wednesday were passed by owners asking $67.00, feedlot sources said.
"If anybody bids $66.00, they're going to own a lot of cattle this morning," one Kansas feedlot operator said.

However, packer buyers were seen waiting out cattle owners as long as possible amid ideas the owners would be willing to sell at $65.00, make a marginal profit and still remain current, the sources said.
Packers reportedly had enough cattle after last week and could hold off buying for another day or two, they said.
Fed cattle prices also could be pressured by concern market-ready cattle numbers will be expanding into the summer.
Prices also were seen vulnerable amid ideas that beef demand during the Memorial Day holiday weekend was stunted by cool, wet weather in much of the central U.S. which curbed outdoor cookouts.
Beef prices on Tuesday were quoted down $0.12 to $0.64 per cwt, with 227 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef on Tuesday was quoted down $0.13 at $104.48, compared with Friday and down $1.55 from a week earlier when prices started crumbling, USDA statistics showed.
